catalog_quote: In Northern Sotho, vowel length is non-contrastive. Hence, it can be used without problems for prosodic purposes. The data in (3-a) show a verb (in i) and an object (in ii) that display a short vowel in penultimate syllable when being followed by a further constituent. A long vowel in penultimate syllable only appears when the word occurs in utterance-final position ... There are only a few idiosyncratic exceptions to this generalization (e.g. the first vowel in maabane- 'yesterday'). ... Length has been equaled with stress in early work by Doke (1927/1992) and has been used as an indicator of word-hood in Bantu languages. A morphological word consequently contains one main stress, i.e. a lengthened syllable. Length at word-level cannot be confirmed for Northern Sotho so far, neither in a preliminary study by Lombard (1979) nor in my own data (see diagram 1). In Northern Sotho, length r…
sweep_summary: Only one distinct work turned up in the title sweep, listed twice by Glottolog: Zerbian 2007, 'Investigating prosodic focus marking in Northern Sotho' (Aboh/Hartmann/Zimmermann eds., Focus Strategies in African Languages, Mouton de Gruyter, pp. 55-82, doi:10.1515/9783110199093.1.55). It is about prosodic focus marking, not word-stress placement, and is a condensed version of ch. 3 of Zerbian's 2006 thesis, which is the catalog's deciding source and is held in full. No open copy exists (Unpaywall closed; not on the author's Stuttgart page, the SFB 632 database, CORE, OpenAlex or fatcat; De Gruyter and Google Books block automated access; the Wayback content service is unreachable from our machine), so it stays paywalled-doi, priority low: the held papers that cite it (Zerbian & Barnard 2010; Turco & Zerbian 2021) use it only for 'focus is not marked prosodically in Sotho-Tswana' and phrase-final tone facts. The catalog coding 'no-word-stress' rests on Zerbian 2006 pp. 109-110 (re-read: word-level length/stress cannot be confirmed; lengthening occurs only at prosodic boundaries above the word), and nothing in this sweep refines or contradicts it.

new_statements.quote: Length has been equaled with stress in early work by Doke (1927/1992) and has been used as an indicator of word-hood in Bantu languages. A morphological word consequently contains one main stress, i.e. a lengthened syllable. Length at word-level cannot be confirmed for Northern Sotho so far, neither in a preliminary study by Lombard (1979) nor in my own data (see diagram 1). In Northern Sotho, length reliably only occurs at prosodic boundaries above the word, but not at the penultimate syllable of every word.
new_statements.citation: Zerbian, Sabine. 2006. Expression of information structure in the Bantu language Northern Sotho. ZAS Papers in Linguistics 45 (PhD thesis, Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin). Sec. 3.2.1 'Penultimate lengthening', pp. 109-110.
new_statements.locator: sec. 3.2.1, p. 110 (txt lines 5565-5570), following Diagram 1 'Penultimate Lengthening in Sepedi'
new_statements.reading: First-hand (own elicitation, PRAAT durations from three Sepedi speakers): the only 'stress'-like cue, penultimate lengthening, is a phrase/utterance-edge phenomenon; there is no word-level length/stress. Consistent with the catalog's 'no-word-stress' coding. This is the catalog's own deciding source re-read in this sweep, not a new source; the only other first-hand text read (Zerbian & Barnard 2010, held, p.2: 'the IP boundaries determine the location of the penultimate lengthening and falling tone which are so salient in the Southern Bantu languages') merely restates it and treats word-level prosody as tone assignment only.
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: title page lines 1-52 confirm ZASPiL 45, Sept 2006, Dissertation Humboldt-Universitaet zu Berlin, so the reader's citation is right). The quoted sentences are verbatim at txt lines 5565-5570, directly after Diagram 1 'Penultimate Lengthening in Sepedi' (lines 5544-5563); the running header '110 CHAPTER 3' is at line 5510 and '3.2. BACKGROUND 111' at line 5571, so the passage is on p.110 of sec. 3.2.1 as stated. Surrounding passage (lines 5487-5489, 5497-5503, 5520-5534): data are Zerbian's own elicitation with five Sepedi speakers; penultimate length appears only utterance-finally, never phrase-medially, with PRAAT relative durations for three speakers. audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: all spans of the deciding quotation and the domain quote are verbatim in the held extracted text of Zerbian 2006 at the stated sections/pages (3.2.1 pp.109-110; 3.3 p.120). sources.quote: 'Sepedi, a South African Bantu tone language. For this language, neither accent nor phrasing seem to be exploited for the prosodic marking of focus' (p.4); fn.3: 'The penultimate syllable of a phrase is always lengthened in Sepedi (Zerbian, 2006).'
sources.note: Recent psycholinguistic study restating 'penultimate syllable of a phrase is always lengthened in Sepedi' and no accentual focus marking. fetched sources now; confirms.

sources.citation: Zerbian, Sabine & Etienne Barnard. 2010. Word-level prosody in Sotho-Tswana. Proceedings of Speech Prosody 2010 (Chicago), paper 062. doi:10.21437/SpeechProsody.2010-62
sources.quote: 'Whereas the IP boundaries determine the location of the penultimate lengthening and falling tone which are so salient in the Southern Bantu languages, the PP boundaries influence the action of tone rules'. Word-level prosody is treated entirely as H/L tone assignment; no word stress is posited.
sources.note: Open follow-up by the deciding author: word-level prosody = tone only; penultimate lengthening located by IP boundaries. fetched sources now; confirms.
